question_text: Two numbers are in ratio 3:5. Their sum is 64. Find the smaller number.

hint_ladder.title: Total parts
hint_ladder.text: The ratio 3:5 means the numbers are divided into 3 + 5 = 8 equal parts.

hint_ladder.title: Value per part
hint_ladder.text: The sum is 64, so each part is worth 64 / 8 = 8.

hint_ladder.title: Smaller number
hint_ladder.text: The smaller number corresponds to 3 parts: 3 × 8 = 24.

hint_ladder.title: Answer
hint_ladder.text: Thus, the smaller number is 24. The larger would be 5 × 8 = 40, and 24 + 40 = 64.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you misapplied the ratio, dividing 64 by 3.2 instead of total parts 8.

C.text: You might have chosen C because you multiplied 3.5 by 8 (3.5×8=28), a common arithmetic slip.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you divided 64 by 2 instead of using the ratio, or confused the larger part with the smaller.

next_time_rule: Key Takeaway: For ratio sum problems, add the parts, divide the sum by total parts, then multiply by the needed part.
deconstruct_text:
Imagine inyong Barangay nag-budget ng 64,000 pesos para sa streetlights at feeding program sa ratio na 3:5. Para malaman ang budget ng mas maliit (streetlights): Total parts = 3+5 = 8. Value per part = 64,000 ÷ 8 = 8,000. Smaller = 3 × 8,000 = 24,000 pesos. Check: La...

Mental Trick (Taglish): 'Mag-add muna ng parts (3+5=8). I-divide ang total (64) sa parts (8) para makuha ang per part (8). Tapos i-multiply sa part ng target (3) para makuha ang sagot (24).' Para hindi malito, tandaan: Add-Divide-Multiply!

**Watch-Out Zone: ratio_total_part_confusion** in action: baka ma-reverse mo ratio.
